chunks: Abdullah ibn al-Nadr ibn Sam'an al-Tamimi narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Makki narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Hasan Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Amr al-Harrani narrated to us, he said: Salih ibn Ziyad narrated to us, he said: Abu Uthman Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Sukkari narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Mu'izz al-Awdi narrated to us, he said: Imran ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Tawus al-Yamani, who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn, the Master of the Worshippers (peace be upon him), used to supplicate with this supplication: My God! By Your glory, Your majesty, and Your greatness!

If I had worshipped You since the creation of my nature from the beginning of time, for the duration of the eternity of Your lordship, with every hair and every blink of an eye throughout perpetual eternity, with the praise and thanks of all creatures combined, I would still have fallen short of expressing gratitude for the most hidden of Your blessings upon me.

And even if I ground the iron ores of the world with my teeth, plowed its earth with the lashes of my eyes, and wept out of fear of You as much blood and pus as the oceans of the heavens and the earths, that would be little compared to the much that is due from Your right upon me.

And even if You, my God, were to punish me after that with the punishment of all creatures combined, and enlarged my form and body for the Fire, and filled Hell and its layers with me, until there was no one punished in the Fire except me, and there was no firewood for Hell other than me, that would still be little for You upon me compared to the much that I have deserved of Your punishment.

key_terms.جلال: Jalal - Majesty, grandeur, magnificence of God

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam Zayn al-Abidin make about divine blessings and humility before God?
ai.summary: This is a deeply moving supplication by Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS), the fourth Imam, renowned for his extraordinary devotion. He expresses the utmost humility before God, declaring that even eternal worship with the combined praise of all creation would fall short of thanking God for His smallest blessing. Tawus al-Yamani, a renowned Tabi'i who witnessed the Imam's devotion firsthand, transmitted this supplication.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Abdullah b. al-Nadr b. Sam`an al-Tamimi narrated to us. He said: Abu’l Qasim Ja`far b. Muhammad al-Makki narrated to us. He said: Abu’l Hasan `Abdulah b. Muhammad b. `Amr al-Harrani narrated to us. He said: Salih b. Ziyad narrated to us. He said: Abu `Uthman `Abdullah b. Maymun al-Sikri narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Mu`iz al-Awadi narrated to us. He said: `Imran b. Salim narrated to us from Tawus al-Yamani.
He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn the Master of Worshipers (as) used to supplicate with this supplication: My God! By Your glory, Your majesty, and Your greatness!

If I had worshiped You forevermore, in the eternity of your lordship, with every hair and glance since I came into existence, with the worship and the thanks of all creatures, I would be lacking in the expression of my thanks for the smallest blessing that You have blessed me with.

Even if I suffered with the iron of this world in my teeth and with its dust smeared on the lashes of my eyes, and I wept as much blood and pus as there is water in the oceans of the heavens and the Earth out of humility before you, that would only be a little from the much that I owe you.

Even if thereafter, You, my God, were to punish me with the punishment of all creatures, and the Fire overcame my form and my body, and I filled the levels of Hell to the point where no one was punished except me, and there would be no firewood in Hell but me, that would only be a little from the much that is due for me from Your punishment.
